note.question: How do opaque selling and inventory management interact in vertically differentiated markets?
note.overview: This paper studies the emerging practice of using opaque selling to dispose of leftover inventory in vertically differentiated markets. With this selling strategy, a firm offers a synthetic product (after the regular selling season) for which consumers do not know the exact identity until after purchase. This opaque-selling strategy is implemented in several industries—for example, travel and retail.

components.formal: Evaluation relation: We refer to the former segment as high-valuation consumers (denoted by subscript h) and the latter segment as low-valuation consumers (denoted by subscript l).
conditions: we assume that highvaluation consumers are more sensitive to quality—that is, Δh > Δl or equivalently ΔH > ΔL.

The firm offers two types of products that differ in quality: a high-quality product (denoted by subscript H) with inventory level KH > 0 and a low-quality product (denoted by subscript L) with inventory level KL > 0.

Furthermore, for each i ∈{h,l} and j ∈{H,L}, we denote Vij as a type-i consumer’s valuation for a type-j product, Δi ≡ViH −ViL as his level of quality sensitivity, and Δj ≡Vhj −Vlj as a highvaluation consumer’s additional benefit (compared with a low-valuation consumer) from a type-j product.
